Parse one step of one workbook, naming why it yielded nothing

Source: R/fiss_parse.R
knw_fiss_parse_step.Rd

Finds the step's sheet, reads it and keeps its wanted rows, keyed by site_key (report_id:reference_number: a reference number is unique only within one submission). Every way a step can yield nothing has a status of its own, so a group's parse log shows each one by name:

Usage

knw_fiss_parse_step(path, report_id, step, cols = knw_fiss_columns()$wanted)

Arguments

path

string, a workbook (.xls or .xlsx).

report_id

string, the submission's EcoCat report id.

step

string, the step (see knw_fiss_match_sheet()).

cols

list, the columns read per step (see knw_fiss_select()).

Value

A list: data, a tibble led by report_id and site_key (NULL unless the status is "ok"), and log, a one-row tibble: report_id, path, step, status, sheet_matched, n_sheet_hits, header_row, banner, rows_raw, rows_after_filter.

Details

  • sheets_error: the workbook's sheets could not be listed;

  • no_sheet_match: no sheet matches the step (tissue data, reach summaries);

  • read_error: reading the sheet failed;

  • empty_sheet: the sheet has no rows;

  • no_header: no "REFERENCE NUMBER" label row in the top 40;

  • no_rows: a header, but no row kept;

  • fish_layout: a Step 2 sheet laid out one row per fish (length_mm and no total_number), whose rows are read as Step 3 instead;

  • ok: rows kept.

Step 3 falls back to the Step 2 sheet when its own sheet gives no rows and the Step 2 sheet is in fish layout: the template ships an empty Step 3 beside whatever was filled in.

Examples

f <- system.file("testdata", "fiss", "individual_fish.xls", package = "knowledge")
# a per-fish sheet named like Step 2 is set aside there and read as Step 3
knw_fiss_parse_step(f, "16389", "step2_fish_coll")$log$status
#> [1] "fish_layout"
s3 <- knw_fiss_parse_step(f, "16389", "step3_indiv_fish")
s3$log[, c("status", "sheet_matched", "header_row")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   status sheet_matched   header_row
#>   <chr>  <chr>                <int>
#> 1 ok     Fish collection          4
s3$data[, c("site_key", "species", "length_mm")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   site_key species length_mm
#>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>    
#> 1 16389:1  RB      95       
#> 2 16389:1  RB      120      
#> 3 16389:2  BT      180
